findings.failure_mode: Any filesystem error (missing file, permissions, ENOENT) panics the thread instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| IOError::ReadFailed(e))? and propagate via a typed error or Result<Vec<Record>, IOError>

findings.failure_mode: A non-numeric field value panics the thread instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Replace with parts[1].parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid)? or equivalent typed error

findings.problem: Lossy `as u16` cast after parse — truncation on values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 value above 65535 silently truncates to u16, corrupting data with no error signal
findings.fix: Use `u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::OutOfRange)?` to reject out-of-range values with a typed error

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] — unchecked indexing into Vec without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: A line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields panics via IndexOut ofBounds
findings.fix: Replace with split_once or get(i) with ok_or(...) to produce a typed parse error for malformed lines

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) — hidden I/O side effect in data-loading function
findings.failure_mode: Pure-appearing function has observable logging side effects, violating functional-core design; makes testing, composability, and audit harder
findings.fix: Move all println!/logging into the imperative shell layer. The core loader should return data only, no console output.

findings.problem: Record uses raw String and u16 — no newtype, no enum, no typestate
findings.failure_mode: Any string is a valid record name; any u16 is a valid value. Illegal domain states are representable. No invariants enforced by the type system.
findings.fix: Introduce newtypes (e.g., RecordName(String) with a smart constructor, or a bounded enum for value categories) and a fallible constructor that rejects empty names and invalid ranges.

findings.problem: load_packets returns Vec<Record> — no error taxonomy at all
findings.failure_mode: All failure modes (I/O error, malformed line, missing field, overflow, allocation) are silently converted to panics with no way to distinguish them
findings.fix: Return `Result<Vec<Record>, PacketError>` where PacketError is an enum with variants like ReadFailed, EmptyInput, Malformed, InvalidValue, Overflow, AllocationFailed

findings.problem: Vec<String> intermediate collection via .collect() without try_reserve or capacity planning
findings.failure_mode: Unbounded allocation growth; on very large files the parser will allocate memory proportional to input size with no capacity bound or allocation-failure handling
findings.fix: If max items is known, call values.try_reserve(max).map_err(|_| PacketError::AllocationFailed)? before collecting. Otherwise use split_once in a streaming loop to avoid the intermediate Vec entirely.

findings.problem: Intermediate Vec<String> allocation for every line — unnecessary heap allocations
findings.failure_mode: Each line allocates 2 String objects (split results), then clones them into Record. For high-throughput packet loading this is a measurable performance cost.
findings.fix: Use `line.split_once(',').ok_or(PacketError::Malformed)?` to get `&str` references, then parse directly into Record fields without intermediate Vec<String> or .clone().

findings.problem: Record fields use owned String instead of borrowed &str or Cow<str>
findings.failure_mode: Every Record owns its name String even when the source data may be short-lived or reused. Wastes memory and prevents zero-copy parsing patterns.
findings.fix: If lifetimes permit (e.g., Record takes &str), use `&str`. Otherwise `Cow<'static, str>` allows zero-copy when input already owns the data.

The function is fundamentally unsafe: every code path that handles real-world input can panic (I/O error, parse error, index out of bounds, numeric overflow via lossy cast, and logging side effects in the core). No error taxonomy, no tests, no benchmarks, no type-level invariants. A production reviewer would block this for all five BLOCKERs before any implementation work.
